summary: This diff is the cumulative change to ai-os/MASTER_INDEX.yaml across the regression (commit a901abb1, which wholesale-replaced the repo-tracked file with the live server copy's content) and its fix (commit 3d2e25ba, already HEAD in this workspace). I independently verified the fix's own claim rather than trusting the commit message: diffing the id set of every `registries:` entry between the pre-regression baseline (c9cea46b) and the current state shows all 50 original repo-only entries are preserved with zero removals, plus 8 new entries legitimately added (7 new `registries:` items plus 1 new `unverified_findings_open_2026_07_22` item), each with plausible, existence-verified, appropriately-hedged content consistent with the file's established style. The file parses cleanly under yaml.safe_load. The unusually large diff stat (2112+/2972-) is mostly attributable to a CRLF-to-LF line-ending normalization that happened somewhere in this commit sequence (the pre-regression blob was 100% CRLF, the current one is 100% LF) plus quick_reference re-serialization/re-indentation, not extensive semantic rewriting. This correctly classifies as tier1 under the deterministic rule (deletions do not exceed 2x insertions; no migrations/schema/auth/security/env paths touched) and does not touch .github/workflows/**. One real but non-blocking defect found: the 7 newly-added `registries:` entries are not reflected in the `quick_reference:` block, which this same file's own header instructions and self_use_task_checklist explicitly require regenerating after any registries edit -- ironic given the task's stated goal of fixing central-entrypoint drift, but it only leaves those 7 entries undiscoverable via the fast-lookup table (no data loss, no misdirection, trivially fixable as a follow-up).
issues: The 7 newly-added registries entries (browser_intent_cache, capability_services_pair, cron_systemd_consolidation_2026_07_29, sap_reports_projexa_completion_effort, umr_tasks_registry, utm_traceability_convention, veri_chat) have no corresponding quick_reference entries, violating this file's own documented regeneration rule -- recommend a fast follow-up task to run generate_quick_reference.py and splice the output back in.
